claim: The remount loop does not dispatch layer actions, leaving overlays missing after a basemap switch.
evidence: When a style switch removes existing overlays, the callback calls layer('disable') and layer('enable') instead of dispatching the atom's action creators. LayerAtom exposes enable/disable actions; the existing applyNewLayerSource implementation uses store.dispatch(layerAtom.disable()) and store.dispatch(layerAtom.enable()) to invoke the renderer lifecycle.

claim: The remount test can pass without any overlay being restored.
evidence: The test substitutes a bare vi.fn() for the layer atom and only checks that it received 'disable'; it never checks enable, renderer mounting, or the restored map layers. This accepts the incorrect atom calls in the implementation.

claim: Each basemap switch adds another settings subscription that persists until map destruction.
evidence: The new callback calls layersOrderManager.init on every switch. init pushes a new layersSettingsAtom.subscribe unsubscribe function into _unsubscribe without removing existing subscriptions; cleanup occurs only in destroy.
